key_insight: TCA-SIR reframes scientific inspiration retrieval as extracting target-conditioned, transferable abstractions rather than ranking papers by topical similarity.
engineering_relevance: This can improve AI-for-Science systems by retrieving sources that better support hypothesis transfer, especially for remote inspirations with reusable principles.
method: Generate a target-conditioned abstraction from each candidate source paper.
Use the learned abstraction representation to score transferability to the target problem.
Return both a ranked retrieval list and an interpretable rationale for why a source transfers.
evidence_signal: On ResearchBench, TCA-SIR outperforms prior SIR methods and direct LLM retrieval, improving HitRate@top4% over MOOSE-Chem by more than 10 percentage points.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of learned abstractions, so weak target conditioning or noisy source text could reduce transferability gains.
paper_title: TCA-SIR: Learning Target-Conditioned Abstractions for Scientific Inspiration Retrieval
